floor_area.verified: Read directly on 2026-11-12: the Samsung C&T E&C Group portfolio gives only the total floor area of the complex, with no floor counts, construction periods or per-building areas. The Samsung Engineering 2021 report gives only the P3 green building capacity and no area figure (about the first two-thirds of the document was read)
floor_area.gov_register: Adjacent facilities confirmed in the building register (Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport): Godeok converter station and substations (Godeok-dong 1730), site 102,076㎡, total floor area 48,546.62㎡; Linde Korea Pyeongtaek plant (Godeok-dong 1722), site 78,833.4㎡, building area 27,316.3㎡, total floor area 22,665.15㎡, 6 buildings, use approval 2023-04-27; sewage and similar treatment facility (Godeok-dong 1721, Samsung 1-ro 60), site 150,297.2㎡, building area 8,429.26㎡, total floor area 21,840.49㎡, use approval 2022-07-15. The Samsung Electronics Pyeongtaek campus is at Godeok-dong 1695 (and 37 other lots; lot number checked on the road-name address site)
floor_area.gov_register_campus: Only two buildings are published in the building register title section for Godeok-dong 1695: (1) Technology building-2 — Samsung-ro 114, building area 6,412.72㎡, total floor area 51,410.10㎡, height 67.90 m, 11 floors above ground and 1 basement, steel-reinforced concrete structure, 16 elevators, permit 2015-02-27, use approval 2026-09-21; (2) North gate building — Samsung 1-ro 457, building area 572.85㎡, total floor area 934.22㎡, height 10.32 m, 2 floors above ground, use approval 2026-04-27. Site area 1,833,839.5㎡. Parking (as registered): about 4,000 indoor self-park spaces, 128,907㎡; about 6,437 outdoor self-park spaces, 172,590㎡. Production facilities such as the FAB, complex and green buildings are not in this public query result. The building-permit per-building summary has 316 entries, but the 100 opened were all temporary structures (containers, etc.). Which box in the model is Technology building-2 was not determined. After the satellite re-reading (v7.13) the Technology building body is about 81 × 42 m (about 3,400㎡), roughly half the registered building area of Technology building-2, so it is hard to regard them as the same building. Public data (facilities subject to mandatory disinfection) list 'Technology building' and 'Technology building 2 (cafeteria on B1–3F)' separately, and the Kakao Map 'Technology building entrance' is at (-387, 2472) northwest of P1. The Kakao Map 'Office building 2' coordinate is inside the Office building 2 box, so Office building 2 and Technology building-2 are judged to be different buildings
floor_area.gov_register_parcels: Register queries by lot in Godeok-dong: 1695 (main campus lot) 2 buildings published; 1696 (Complex 2) 1 parking building published; 1697, 1698, 1699, 1725, 1727 and 1728 no result. Office buildings 1, 2 and 3, the office complex building, the welfare building and the FAB buildings are not in the public query results
floor_area.map_crosscheck: Google Maps vs. Kakao Map (2026-11-12): the office complex building, GATE2 and GATE3 agree within 15 m. GATE5 differs by about 235 m between Kakao Map (494, 828) and Google (306, 686), so both points are kept as markers (which is right is unconfirmed). Places only on Google: Technology building; P2 parking tower and open-air parking (Godeok-dong 1696). Public data (facilities subject to mandatory disinfection): T1 cafeteria = Technology building 1F; T2 cafeteria = Technology building 2, B1–3F — the two are registered as separate adjacent buildings. Naver Map could not be checked because access was blocked
floor_area.planned: Filing (2026-07): Pyeongtaek Complex 2 ancillary buildings group 2 — three buildings (resource recirculation centre, oil-water separator, disaster prevention centre), total floor area 2,774 pyeong, until 2027-10-31. Location unknown, not modelled
floor_area.verified2: Further reading on 2026-11-12: Samsung Electronics Sustainability Report 2026 (full text) — no table of site or building areas by site and no Pyeongtaek-only figure (only the total for 5 domestic sites). Samsung E&A P1 Utility Project page — title and year (2018) only. Samsung C&T quarterly report PDF — body could not be read (returned as binary)

reference_press.P2: about 250,000 pyeong; 592,077㎡ published by the construction supervisor (1 basement to 8 floors above ground)

floor_area.check: P2 official value 128,900㎡ ÷ model plan (552 × 204 m = about 112,600㎡) = 1.14. The official wording is 'total floor area', but it is far smaller than the sum of eight floors (590,000㎡ per the construction supervisor) and is close to a single-floor plan. The model plan may be about 13% small, or the official value may include ancillary parts (unconfirmed)

meta.source_policy: Source priority: (1) official material and filings of Samsung Electronics and its contractors, and public registers; (2) international wire services and trade media outside Korea (Reuters, TrendForce, DIGITIMES, etc.); (3) Korean press. Where one fact has several sources, the higher tier is listed first. International outlets often cite Korean reports, so the original report is kept alongside

products.rule: Only what appears in Samsung Electronics official announcements and press is listed. The zone inside a building is given only where it is public; otherwise it is marked 'zone not public'. Product mix changes often with demand, so read each entry with its date
rows: Press on a P1 tour (2022-09): advanced DRAM and NAND are made here. Press 2025-11: a mixed NAND/DRAM line, with conversion of part of NAND to DRAM under review

Samsung Electronics official (2020-08): started with EUV 1z LPDDR5 DRAM, as a combined line that also makes V-NAND and foundry products. Foundry line construction started 2020-05, NAND line 2020-06. Press 2026-03: 4, 5 and 7 nm foundry lines operating in P2 and P3
Press on a Samsung Electronics announcement (2022-09): NAND first, with wafer input from 2022-07, then DRAM and foundry in turn
Press: 'PH2 of P3, an existing foundry line'. Press also reports a bridge installed to link it with P4 PH2
Press: the cleanroom is split in half between NAND and DRAM. Reports differ on the DRAM generation (1a in one, 1c in another)
Press: a 1c DRAM-only line. One report says dividing the 300 m cleanroom into two or three sections for different product lines was discussed
Press: being built as a DRAM-only space
Press: changed from an original foundry/memory hybrid plan to a 1c DRAM line (decided 2025-12). Main construction from 2026 Q2, ready for operation targeted for the first half of 2027 (plan)
HBM and DRAM focus (mix not finalized)
Press (2026-02): planned with three levels so that HBM, DRAM and foundry can be allocated by level; product mix not finalized

levels: Dry pumps, scrubbers, chillers, chemical supply, transformers and distribution. The level that keeps contamination and heat sources away from the cleanroom
Directly below the tools. RF generators and power racks, gas boxes and VMBs, pipe laterals. Return space through which air from the cleanroom passes
Process tools, stockers, OHT. Tools on a raised access floor, FFUs in the ceiling. P1 has a visitor window corridor on 3F (press)
Supply space that feeds air down to the FFUs. Make-up air units (MAU), DCC, structural trusses
Pumps, scrubbers and chillers for the upper cleanroom; chemical and power distribution
Power racks and gas boxes directly below the upper cleanroom
Supply space for the upper cleanroom; MAU and DCC
Exhaust scrubbers, fans and stacks; pipe racks. The perimeter band is higher than the central roof (drone video)

elems.name: Technology building (Google Maps label; not confirmed to be the same building as 'Technology building-2' in the register)
elems.note: An earlier version guessed this was Office building 1, but the Kakao Map 'Office building 1' label point is on the west building, so that guess was withdrawn. Plan measured from satellite imagery; height and use are estimates. Corners were re-read from satellite imagery (Esri World Imagery, zoom 18, about 0.48 m/px, re-acquired 2026-11-12) to reset plan and orientation (reading error about ±5 m). Up to v7.12 the orientation was reversed (−30°) and the plan was 86 × 80 m including the dark accessory part to the east — corrected to the main body with the visible solar roof, about 81 × 42 m, oriented 38° toward the northeast. The Google Maps place 'Samsung Electronics Pyeongtaek Campus Technology Building' (37.04006, 127.05605 → about (-351, 2231) in the model) falls inside this box. Kakao Map labels a point about 240 m to the north 'Technology building entrance' and the building to the east 'Technology building parking tower'. The building register publishes only 'Technology building-2' (building area 6,412.72㎡, height 67.90 m, 11 floors above ground); whether that is this building is not determined, because 'Technology building' and 'Technology building 2' are registered separately in public data and the plan of this box (about 3,400㎡) is much smaller. Press: Office building 1 (for P1) has 9 floors and Office building 2 (for P2) has 11 floors; office and production buildings are sited separately

elems.name: Large southeast annex S1 (green building / water treatment, est.)
elems.note: Plan measured from satellite imagery; height and use are estimates. Press: P4 consists of four facilities — FAB building, complex building, substation and green building (wastewater treatment) — and the green building is built by Samsung Engineering. Samsung E&A contract names in filings include the green building, and Hansung Cleantech disclosed an order for mechanical and piping installation in the P4 green building. The existence and use of the green building are confirmed; its match to this building is not. Reference (official disclosure, 2021): the underground water treatment facility of the Pyeongtaek green building has a footprint of about 34,000㎡, purifies about 70,000 t a day, treats wastewater in six streams by composition, has screen doors on chemical piping, a central control room (CCR) and a 97% automation rate. The plan of this box is about 28,000㎡

elems.name: Godeok converter station (building register; building match estimated by area comparison)

Building register (Godeok-dong 1730, Samsung 1-ro 160 — building name 'Godeok converter station, Godeok substation #1, Godeok substation #2'): site 102,076㎡, 3 main buildings and 6 accessory buildings, permit 2014-12-24, construction start 2015-04-13, use approval 2024-10-02. Excluding the partitioned bays on both sides of the south block (which appear to be transformer bays) the figures match, so this building is taken to be the converter station

elems.name: Ultrapure water (UPW) production plant (concept)
elems.note: Generic reference design (concept). Not the actual location, count or capacity of equipment at the Pyeongtaek campus. Pretreatment → reverse osmosis, ion exchange, degassing → storage → polishing. Press reports that Samsung Engineering handled P3 UPW, but the location is unconfirmed

elems.name: Reclaimed-water recovery plant (concept)

elems.name: Chemical tanker unloading bay (transfer after quality check) — filling point (concept)
elems.note: Connection where chemicals are transferred from a tanker to the storage tank. A containment dike, leak detection and quality check are typical. Location is an arbitrary concept marker

elems.name: UT building rooftop cooling tower area (est.)
elems.note: Water vapour seen above the utility building between P3 and P4 in satellite imagery. Cell count and extent are assumed

elems.name: Bulk gas receiving and backup yard (concept, arbitrary location)
elems.note: Press: bulk gases are supplied through underground pipelines from gas-company plants to the south. The backup storage location inside the campus is not public, so only a concept is shown at an arbitrary location

elems.name: Bulk gas tanker transfer connection — filling point (concept)
elems.note: Connection where a liquefied-gas tanker transfers gas into the storage tank. A different task from the cylinder exchange area. Location is an arbitrary concept marker

elems.name: Direction of the Air First Pyeongtaek plant (about 1 km south; supply to P3 and P4 per press) — concept entry point
elems.note: The Kakao Map location of the Air First Pyeongtaek plant is about (-413, -278) in model coordinates, south of the campus. Press: about 1 km in a straight line from the campus, supplying oxygen, nitrogen, argon and hydrogen by underground pipeline, serving P3 and P4. Entry point and route are not public

elems.name: Direction of the Air Products Korea Pyeongtaek plant (adjacent to the northeast; supply to P1 per press) — concept entry point
elems.note: The Kakao Map location of the Air Products Korea Pyeongtaek plant is about (624, 2220), immediately northeast of the campus (there is also an 'Air Products intersection' place name). Press: supplies industrial gases to Pyeongtaek campus fab 1. Pipeline route is not public

elems.name: Direction of the Linde Korea Pyeongtaek plant (southwest, press) — concept entry point
elems.note: The Kakao Map location of the Linde Korea Pyeongtaek plant is about (-906, 776), southwest of the campus. Building register (Godeok-dong 1722): site 78,833.4㎡, building area 27,316.3㎡, total floor area 22,665.15㎡, 6 main buildings, construction start 2018-11-20, use approval 2023-04-27. Press: has worked with the Pyeongtaek campus since its early days; Pyeongtaek is Linde's largest single site for the electronics industry. Pipeline route is not public

elems.name: Direction of the 345 kV Godeok–Seoanseong transmission line (east, 23.5 km, press) — concept point
elems.note: Press: 10.2 km overhead (35 towers) + 13.3 km underground, completed 2023-09-12, supply capacity 2 GW for P1–P4, construction cost of about KRW 390 billion borne by Samsung Electronics. OSM records a 345 kV underground cable arriving from the east. The substation entry point is a concept marker

elems.name: Direction of the 500 kV Bukdangjin–Godeok HVDC link (west, 34.2 km underground, press) — concept point
elems.note: Press: HVDC link sending 3 GW of generation from the Dangjin area to the southern Seoul metropolitan area including Pyeongtaek (stage 1, 1.5 GW, 2020-12). Converter station at Godeok. The entry point is a concept marker

elems.name: Campus power receiving and main transformer equipment (estimated location of the 154 building; equipment is concept)
elems.note: Generic reference design (concept). Not the actual location, count or capacity of equipment at the Pyeongtaek campus. Equipment that steps power received from the KEPCO substation down to campus distribution voltage. The campus receiving voltage was not confirmed from public sources. In v7 the location was moved to match the '154 building (substation)' in a captioned photo from a site-observation channel (a separate building southeast of the P4 fab). The internal equipment form and the route to the KEPCO substation are concept

elems.name: Employee parking lot (Kakao Map label; OSM boundary)
elems.note: Confirmed from the OpenStreetMap parking boundary and parked vehicles in satellite imagery

elems.name: Parking-lot solar canopy (existence: official material; location: est.)
elems.note: Sustainability reports: 0.4 MW of solar at the Pyeongtaek site (2021 and 2022 reports), 0.2 MW added in 2022, 0.7 MW (2024 report). Press: panels are installed over parking lots at semiconductor sites and are not used for production lines. This location is an estimate from a blue-grey roof (about 65 × 44 m) southwest of the parking lot in satellite imagery; that it is solar was not confirmed

elems.name: Industrial water intake (regional waterworks, Paldang system, press) — arbitrary point
elems.note: Press: the Pyeongtaek campus receives 220,000 t of industrial water a day (with fabs 1 and 2 operating; press 2020 and 2024). Water for Giheung, Hwaseong and Pyeongtaek is taken from the Han River at Paldang (press 2022). The entry point and pipeline into the campus are not public

elems.name: Sewage-reclaimed water intake (Suwon, Hwaseong, Osan; planned around 2030) — arbitrary point
elems.note: Press: plan to supply 372,000 t a day to the Godeok (Pyeongtaek) site — Suwon 280,000 t, Hwaseong Dongtan 2 42,000 t, Osan 50,000 t — through a dedicated pipeline of about 60 km. As of press in 2026-09, about 120,000 t from Hwaseong and Osan and about 210,000 t from Suwon were in preparation. A plan, not yet in supply

elems.name: Treated-effluent discharge boundary (press: Pyeongtaek public wastewater treatment plant → Seojeongni stream)
elems.note: Press (as of 2020): the Pyeongtaek campus used about 67,000 t of water a day on average, and about 54,000 t was discharged to Seojeongni stream via the Pyeongtaek city wastewater treatment plant. Building register: 'sewage and similar treatment facility' at Godeok-dong 1721 (Samsung 1-ro 60) — site 150,297.2㎡, building area 8,429.26㎡, total floor area 21,840.49㎡, use approval 2022-07-15. The register alone does not establish that this is the Godeok public wastewater treatment plant named in the press. Path (press on a Gyeonggi Province inspection, 2026-10): on-site water treatment 'green building' (primary treatment) → Godeok public wastewater treatment plant → Seojeongni stream → Jinwi stream → Anseong stream → Pyeongtaek lake. The 17 PFAS reported by a civic group in 2026-10 came from a sample taken at the final outlet of the Godeok industrial complex public wastewater treatment plant (Godeok-dong 2745, Seojeongni stream); press reports note that this plant also receives treated water from facilities other than Samsung Electronics, so the whole amount cannot be attributed to Samsung Electronics. Samsung Electronics plan (press): pilot unit for PFAS separation/concentration followed by electrochemical treatment to be installed 2026-12 and applied 2027-08. The effluent temperature-reduction facility uses thermal-energy recovery rather than cooling towers, targeting about 30 ℃ → 17 ℃ or below, with commissioning 2026-12 to 2027-02. The locations of the temperature-reduction facility and the pilot unit are not public and are not modelled. This box is a concept marker, not the coordinates of the actual outlet

elems.name: Samsung Electronics logistics warehouse — relocation planned (Kakao Map label · read from imagery · presumed CDC logistics centre; press reports a move to the new Poseung CDC)
elems.note: Plan measured from satellite imagery; height and use are estimates. Plan read from satellite imagery (Esri World Imagery, zoom 18, about 0.48 m/px, re-acquired 2026-11-13) with an error of about ±5 m. Cylindrical tanks and process equipment are simplified as boxes. The building Kakao Map labels 'Samsung Electronics logistics warehouse' (logistics centre, Godeok-dong 1696-1). In the 2025-12-22 satellite imagery it is a single-roof building of about 177 × 320 m (about 56,600㎡) with rows of loading docks on its east and west sides. Height estimated at about 21 m from the shadow length (about 37 m). No entry was returned by the public building register. Press (2025-12): the CDC logistics centre on the planned P6 site is to be demolished by May 2026, and the demolition permit has been issued. A CDC (Central Distribution Center) is a central logistics centre that handles receiving, storage, sorting and delivery of products; Samsung Electronics is building a home-appliance CDC of about 110,000㎡ in the Pyeongtaek Poseung district (started 2025-03, completion targeted 2027-06; investment agreement reported 2026-09). Read together, the reports describe a product distribution centre rather than a fab materials warehouse, and a relocation to Poseung rather than a closure. However, no source states directly that this Kakao Map building is the CDC in the press, or that the Poseung centre replaces it, so both are inferences; whether it has been demolished was not confirmed. Further checks (press 2020): the Samsung Electronics Pyeongtaek integrated logistics centre (CDC) was completed in 2018, handles logistics for most Samsung home appliances such as TVs, refrigerators and air conditioners, and is managed by the subsidiary Samsung Electronics Logitech. In 2025-12 another outlet also reported the plan to demolish the CDC on the planned P6 site and that the permit had been obtained. The Poseung centre is expected to distribute appliances made in Korea and products made abroad arriving through Pyeongtaek port (press 2026-09). Press in 2026: the fab after P5 is planned as a twin fab with the same structure as P5 (P5-2), and site workers say excavation has started — this is not direct confirmation that this building has been demolished. A layout graphic made by a YouTube real-estate channel (2026-09, watched muted) draws P5 Fab 2 immediately north of P5 Fab 1, and this warehouse falls in its north-west corner — it is not an official drawing and is used only as a reference. This model therefore labels the building as relocation planned

Condenser water supply (cooling tower → chiller condenser)
Heat-recovery hot water (optional system: condenser heat → MAU reheat/preheat)
Process cooling water supply (heat exchanger → tools, pumps, scrubbers)
Bulk gas (N2, O2, Ar, H2, etc.: pipeline from external plants → purification → CSF header)
Specialty gas (gas cabinet / BSGS → VMB → tool)
Acid exhaust (→ central wet scrubber → stack)
Organic (VOC/solvent) exhaust (→ zeolite concentrator rotor + oxidizer)
Treated effluent discharge (green building → public wastewater treatment plant → stream)
Chemical supply (tanker unloading and ACQC → storage → CCSS → VMB)
Reclaimed-water recovery (low-concentration rinse drain → recovery plant)
Industrial water intake (regional waterworks, Paldang system, press)
Sewage-reclaimed water intake (Suwon, Hwaseong, Osan; planned around 2030, press)

Emergency power (emergency generators → selected emergency loads)
Parking-lot solar (used on site, not for production lines — press)

ugroups.title: Thermal management: chillers · cooling towers · chilled water · MAU · DCC · waste-heat recovery
flow: Chiller evaporator ↔ chilled water (CHW) supply/return ↔ MAU cooling and dehumidifying coils / DCC (sensible heat removal) / primary side of PCW heat exchangers
Chiller condenser ↔ condenser water (CW) supply/return ↔ cooling tower (heat rejected to atmosphere)
Air: outdoor air → MAU (preheat, humidify, cool/dehumidify, reheat) → plenum → FFU → cleanroom → below the floor → DCC in the return shaft → plenum
Optional: condenser heat and return-water heat → heat-recovery chiller / heat exchanger → hot water for MAU reheat and winter preheat
values: Chilled water for MAU cooling coils about 5–7 °C (paper); in dual-temperature chilled water systems, low temperature about 6–7 °C (MAU) and high temperature about 15–18 °C (DCC) (company technical article)
MAU sequence in the literature: fan → preheat coil → precool coil → humidifier (air washer) → cooling coil → reheat coil
The DCC runs with the coil surface above the return-air dew point so that no condensation forms (hence 'dry')
site: Satellite imagery shows the fan cell arrays of the four cooling tower banks east of P1 and P2, and water vapour over the utility building between P3 and P4 and the north utility area (grades B and C)
Disclosed and reported: Samsung E&A performed the Pyeongtaek P2 UT building and the P3 green building, UT building, rooftop exhaust and UPW (grade A: existence)
'P4 Ph4 DCC section 1' appears in a contract name in a filing (grade A: existence of DCC work)

Samsung Electronics Sustainability Report (2023): at Giheung, Hwaseong and Pyeongtaek, waste heat from equipment cooling water and wastewater effluent is recovered and reused as a heat source for process water and HVAC (grade A: existence of waste-heat recovery)
Geothermal heating/cooling at the Pyeongtaek site: 200 RT (2021 and 2022 reports) → 738 RT (2023 report). Installed under some buildings at Hwaseong and Pyeongtaek (press). Location is not public
ugroups.limit: Chiller type, count and capacity, chilled water temperature set points, whether waste-heat recovery is applied, and actual pipe routes are not public. Placing chillers in the utility building and the fab connection points are assumptions. Chilled water headers are placed in the return-shaft bands and the central core and do not cross above the FFU ceiling (whether this reduces the risk of water leaks falling into the cleanroom is a review hypothesis).

ugroups.title: PCW: process cooling water closed loop
flow: PCW heat exchanger (secondary side) → circulation pump → supply header → bay branches → tools, dry pumps, scrubbers, RF power → return header → heat exchanger
The primary side of the heat exchanger is chilled water (CHW) or cooling tower water. PCW is a closed loop dedicated to tools; it is not consumed or discharged in normal operation
values: Required temperature in the literature about 13–20 °C (paper)
Measured benchmark case (a fab in Taiwan): supply 17.8 °C, return 21 °C, flow 1,121.9 ㎥/h, cooling capacity 1,187 RT
Check: Q = ρ·V·cp·ΔT = 1000 × (1121.9/3600) × 4.186 × 3.2 ≈ 4,175 kW ≈ 1,187 RT (3.517 kW/RT) → matches the literature figure
site: PCW temperature, flow and redundancy for Pyeongtaek P1–P4 could not be confirmed from public sources.
ugroups.limit: Heat exchanger locations (1F and 5F FSF support zones) and header and branch positions are all concept. This is not the result of a hydraulic analysis with pipe sizing or flow calculation.

ugroups.title: Gas: bulk gas · specialty gas · filling (transfer) and exchange points
flow: Bulk gas: nearby gas-company plant (air separation unit) → underground pipeline → campus entry → (backup liquid storage and vaporization) → purification → fab CSF header → tools
Specialty gas: delivery of cylinders and bulk containers → gas cabinet or BSGS → distribution (VMB) → tool gas box. Purge and cabinet exhaust are separate systems
Distinction of tasks: bulk storage has a 'transfer/filling connection'; cylinders have an 'exchange work area' (cylinders are not filled on site)
values: Figures such as pressure, purity and storage quantity vary by supplier and process and are not included in this model (unsupported figures excluded).
site: Newsis site article, 2022-09: the campus has a large GCS (Gas Chemical System) building storing the gases and chemicals used in production, which are supplied to the production lines through connecting bridges only when needed, for safety (grade A: existence of the GCS building and supply bridges; the article does not say which building)
Gas supply for P1–P4 is split among Air Products, Linde and Air First (press). P1 is Air Products Korea (press); the P3 bulk gas supplier is Air First (press)
The Air First Pyeongtaek plant (about 200,000㎡) is about 1 km in a straight line from the campus and supplies oxygen, nitrogen, argon and hydrogen by underground pipeline (press 2026-05)
Linde announced an eighth air separation unit at Pyeongtaek for additional ultra-high-purity gases and hydrogen (press)
'P4 Ph4 S-GAS section 1' appears in a contract name in a filing (existence of specialty-gas work)

Plant locations of the three gas companies (Kakao Map): Air Products Korea immediately northeast of the campus, Linde Korea to the southwest, Air First about 1 km to the south → entries from three directions are shown
Linde Korea, Air First and Air Products Korea are also due to move into the Pyeongtaek Advanced Complex General Industrial Park, 460,000㎡ around Bangchuk-ri, Godeok-myeon, south of the campus (press)

Pyeongtaek city supplies treated water from the Godeok public sewage treatment plant to these three gas companies as industrial cooling water: 3.23 km pipeline, 50 cm diameter, 24,400 t a day planned (press 2026-10)
ugroups.limit: Storage locations inside the campus, entry points, pipe routes and gas-room locations are not public. The yard, gas rooms and mains are concept markers at arbitrary locations.

ugroups.title: Hazardous emissions (air): exhaust segregation and treatment
flow: Process tool → (where needed) dry pump and POU treatment → dedicated exhaust header matching the stream → central treatment equipment → fan → stack (treated exhaust)
Segregation: acid / alkali (ammonia) / organic (VOC, solvent) / heat and general. Mixing causes reactions and solids, so they are collected separately
POU → rooftop scrubber → stack is one of several arrangements; the type and presence of POU depend on the process
values: Exhaust classification in the literature: heat/general / acid / (optional) ammonia / VOC. Heat exhaust is often released without treatment (patent literature)
VOC: zeolite concentrator rotor + thermal oxidizer; acid and alkali: central wet scrubber (paper)
Acid gases are treated in wet scrubbers by contact with a neutralizing solution (vendor technical material)
site: Press that Samsung Engineering handled P3 'rooftop exhaust' (grade A: existence of rooftop exhaust equipment)
Satellite and drone imagery shows steel racks and rows of equipment on the fab rooftop perimeter bands (grades B and C)

Samsung Electronics Sustainability Report (2023): semiconductor sites abate process gases (F-gases) with POU scrubbers and rooftop RCS (regenerative catalytic systems) (grade A: existence of the equipment type; count and location at Pyeongtaek not public)
ugroups.limit: Which system is on which rack, and the type, count and efficiency of treatment equipment, are not public. South = acid/alkali and north = organic/heat is an assumption for explanation (one review opinion holds that an east/west split may shorten routes, but this is unsupported).

ugroups.title: Hazardous emissions (water): segregated collection and treatment of wastewater
flow: Sources (cleaning, CMP, scrubber drains) → segregated collection by composition (fluoride / acid-alkali / organic …) → transfer by stream → the corresponding treatment stage in the green building
Treated water → public wastewater treatment plant → discharge to stream. Part is reused on site
values: Treatment process figures (chemical doses, retention time, etc.) are not included.
site: Introduction to an official Samsung Semiconductor video (series Ep. 5): the Pyeongtaek campus wastewater plant has a '2.6 km underground passage', screen doors that prevent leaks and a 24-hour control room (grade A: existence of the underground passage; route not public)
The Pyeongtaek campus has two green buildings, an underground water treatment area of about 34,000㎡, purifies about 70,000 t a day on average, and about 97% of the work is automated (press 2021)
As of 2020 the Pyeongtaek campus used about 67,000 t a day on average, and about 54,000 t was discharged to Seojeongni stream via the Pyeongtaek city wastewater treatment plant (press)
Samsung Electronics company-wide water flow in 2024 (thousand t): surface water 187,626 → on-site treatment 59,569 and off-site treatment 92,540; reuse 125,463 (sustainability data)

ugroups.title: Chemical supply: unloading · storage · central supply (CCSS)
flow: Tanker unloading bay (quality check) → storage tank → central chemical supply system (CCSS) → double-contained piping → supply unit in the fab FSF → distribution (VMB) → clean and track tools
CMP slurry is supplied in a loop that keeps circulating from the supply room to near the tool to prevent settling
values: Pressure, flow velocity and purity figures are not included.
site: Press citing a brokerage report: STI CCSS was supplied to Pyeongtaek fab 3 Ph3 and Ph4 and fab 4 Ph1 and Ph2
Hanyang ENG disclosed a P5 piping contract (press 2026-09)
ugroups.limit: The unloading bay, storage location and pipe routes are not public. Placement at the west end of the utility building is arbitrary.

ugroups.title: Ultrapure water (UPW) and reclaimed water
flow: Industrial water → pretreatment → reverse osmosis, ion exchange, degassing → UPW storage → polishing → fab circulation loop (supply/return) → tools
Low-concentration rinse drain is collected separately and reused via a recovery plant (returned to raw water or utility water, not directly to UPW)
values: Water quality and recovery-rate figures are not included.
site: The Pyeongtaek campus (with fabs 1 and 2 operating) receives 220,000 t of industrial water a day and would need a further 250,000 t a day with up to fab 6 operating (press 2020 and 2024). Raw water is from the Han River Paldang system (press 2022: about 300,000 t a day in total for Giheung, Hwaseong and Pyeongtaek is taken at Paldang)

Options for additional water (press 2020): additional supply by K-water (Paldang and Chungju dams; over KRW 1 trillion and over 10 years) or development of Pyeongtaek city's own source (Anseong stream; KRW 334.8 billion, 7 years)

Sewage reuse plan (press 2022): Suwon 280,000 t, Hwaseong Dongtan 2 42,000 t, Osan 50,000 t = 372,000 t a day to the Godeok (Pyeongtaek) site, dedicated pipeline about 60 km, about KRW 600 billion, from 2030

Industrial water use at the Pyeongtaek campus: about 120,000 t a day as of November 2022 (local press)
Agreement of 2022-11: plan to supply 372,000 t a day of treated sewage from Suwon, Hwaseong and Osan to the Pyeongtaek campus and 102,000 t to Giheung and Hwaseong (474,000 t in total)
Press that Samsung Engineering handled P3 UPW (grade A: existence)
ugroups.limit: The location, capacity and loop arrangement of the UPW plant are not public. Placement in the utility building is an assumption. The points where industrial and reclaimed water enter the campus and the pipeline routes are also not public and are marked arbitrarily on the north boundary. The press figures (220,000 t and 120,000 t) differ in date and basis (supply vs. use).

ugroups.title: Power: receiving · transformation · distribution · UPS · emergency power
flow: KEPCO transmission grid (345 kV and 154 kV) → receiving and transformation (GIS, main transformers) → medium-voltage distribution (dual feeders) → fab electrical-room transformers → low-voltage switchboards and busduct → loads
Selected critical loads ← UPS and voltage-sag compensation / selected emergency loads ← transfer equipment ← emergency generators
UPS and emergency generators do not carry the whole fab process load
values: The campus distribution voltage (22.9 kV) assumes the usual Korean medium-voltage distribution level; the site value was not confirmed.
site: The KEPCO Godeok substation is across one road from the campus, has 1 basement and 4 floors above ground and a total floor area of about 100,000㎡, supplies 345 kV, with substation 1 operating from 2016 and substation 2 from 2022, on land provided by Samsung (Seoul Economic Daily, 2024-12). OpenStreetMap also records a 'Godeok substation' lot and three buildings south of P4, and the model location was corrected to that boundary (grades A and B)
